purpose: Give an AI orchestrator an explicit execution policy for every roadmap-like artifact without rewriting historical evidence files.

authority.conflict_rule: Current dated completion and gate evidence wins over stale queue prose. A recommendation in the June structured seed is not claimable until reconciled with the July open-work and runner state. Never infer that an old unchecked or next-slice line reopens completed work.

findings: The previous safe repository queue was exhausted, but the operator opened normalized TAX/TUA post-MVP roadmaps on 2026-07-13. Their scoped repo-only slices are now the current safe queue and do not reopen the fixed ten-roadmap MVP runner.
Several old roadmaps retain active or in-progress wording after their slices were completed or superseded. Current evidence must outrank old queue prose.
Multi-agent throughput is constrained mainly by shared UI, Telegram, planning and runtime hot files. Read-only scouts scale safely; write agents require disjoint path claims.
Master roadmaps and runner state are routers, not worker tasks. They require one orchestrator writer and report reduction from workers.

GMI and GRO are runtime execution and observability tracks only. USI owns index identity, CBM is a rebuildable codegraph provider, Git/Project Versioning owns history, and Lens Code is a UI consumer; no one track may absorb the others.

The normalized USI/CBM/Lineage/Lens roadmaps are planned follow-ups and do not replace the current TAX/TUA queue. On a future goal, only each roadmap's first declared slice becomes claimable. Productive CBM, Lineage and Lens activation remains independently gated; the UIR/UDA/ULO child closures share the parent USI gate.

USI core is not activation-complete without its three child closures: UIR owns composition and consumers, UDA owns policy-aware domain adapters and best-effort change signals, and ULO owns index participation in existing owner/data lifecycle operations. None may absorb domain truth, existing operations, TAX/TUA, GRO/GMI, CBM/Lineage or Lens ownership.
Clarification is a planning precondition for the Harbor One autonomous workspace; missing product decisions must be asked, not inferred.

canonical_router.parallelism: Read-only scouts may run in parallel; only the orchestrator may reduce reports, change queue state, accept claims, or mutate the router artifact.
required_behavior: Reconcile all candidate work with the current gate and completion authorities before dispatch.
Require a claim or lease and reject overlapping allowed paths.
Do not execute a router, master plan, or runner state as if it were an implementation slice.

active_parallel.parallelism: Alice, Bob, and Charlie may work concurrently only when slice dependencies are satisfied and allowed paths do not overlap. Charlie owns integration.
required_behavior: Claim one explicit slice with class, owner, allowed paths, tests, evidence, and gate.
Serialize shared hot files and any path omitted from the slice contract.
Stop at live, design, provider, data, deploy, or destructive gates.

active_serial.parallelism: Parallel work is limited to read-only audits or design alternatives; one accepted owner writes after the orchestrator resolves dependencies and hot files.
required_behavior: Freeze a current slice and allowed paths before editing.
Do not let multiple workers edit shared UI, plugin, runtime, or roadmap hot files.
Use a handoff and fresh tests before the next writer starts.

gate_only.parallelism: Read-only evidence collection may run in parallel. Gate execution is one bounded operator-approved action at a time.
required_behavior: Do not invent backend cleanup or implementation slices to avoid the gate.
Prepare a decision packet with target, safe default, evidence path, forbidden actions, and rollback or stop rule.
Never claim live completion from repo tests or dry-run evidence.

historical_done.parallelism: No implementation dispatch. Scouts may cite verified evidence or compare it with current code.
required_behavior: Do not reopen completed slices or overwrite historical evidence.
Route new work to a current roadmap or create a new normalized follow-up.
Treat deferred ideas as unapproved, not as an active queue.

needs_normalization.parallelism: Multiple read-only scouts may inspect code, tests, and newer plans; no worker writes implementation until one orchestrator publishes a current status and scoped queue.
required_behavior: Resolve contradictory status, stale next-slice text, and superseding roadmaps first.
Add or select an explicit owner, allowed paths, tests, dependencies, and gate before dispatch.
If normalization needs product intent, ask the user instead of interpreting the gap.
